## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed heat-safety program for outdoor workers that would combine hyper-local heat alerts, cooled rest shelters, and simple rules employers must follow on dangerous days.

## Problem

Outdoor workers in construction, delivery, and landscaping face serious health risks during extreme heat. General weather warnings are not specific enough to a worksite, and many workers feel unable to stop and rest without losing income.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Construction workers, delivery riders, cleaners, and gardeners who work outdoors, and the small employers who hire them. A delivery rider would receive an alert on a very hot afternoon showing the nearest cooled rest point.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes a heat-risk map combining temperature and humidity at neighborhood level, a network of cooled rest shelters at key locations such as fuel stations and parks, and a mobile alert for workers and employers. On high-risk days, employers would be asked to apply mandatory rest breaks, with guidance published in several languages.

## Delivery Model

Shelters would be proposed through partnerships with private sites, and alerts would go through a lightweight app and SMS. Inspectors would do spot checks on high-risk days.

## Funding & Sustainability

The plan is a shared model: the government would fund the alert system and a first set of shelters, and larger employers would be invited to sponsor additional shelters.

## What Makes It New

It moves from general weather warnings to worksite-level risk and pairs every alert with a practical place to rest.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include heat-related clinic visits among outdoor workers, shelter usage, and employer compliance on alert days.

## Risks & Mitigation

Workers may ignore alerts if they fear losing pay; the initiative plans to publish clear employer obligations. Shelter maintenance costs would be tested in a first phase.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed home rehabilitation service where patients recovering from surgery or stroke would do guided physiotherapy at home through video sessions and simple motion-tracking on a phone.

## Problem

Many patients stop attending physiotherapy because travelling to a clinic several times a week is tiring, expensive, or impossible without help. Incomplete rehabilitation leads to slower recovery and more hospital readmissions.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or stroke, especially elderly patients and people living far from clinics, and the family members who support them.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes weekly live video sessions with a physiotherapist, plus daily exercises guided by a phone app that would use the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan.

## Delivery Model

Delivered by public hospital physiotherapy departments, with devices lent to patients who lack a smartphone.

## Funding & Sustainability

The initiative plans to be funded within existing hospital budgets, with the aim of lowering costs from readmissions and transport.

## What Makes It New

It brings rehabilitation into the home and uses the phone camera as a coach between sessions.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include completion rates of rehabilitation plans, mobility scores, and readmissions within 90 days, compared with clinic-based care in a planned trial.

## Risks & Mitigation

Some patients may struggle with technology; the plan is a first home visit to set up the device and train a family member.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed service that detects life events such as the birth of a child, job loss, or retirement and would offer eligible families the relevant government support automatically, without an application.

## Problem

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems.

## Delivery Model

The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A small central team would maintain the eligibility rules, and each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability

The initiative plans to be funded from the existing social support budget, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced application processing and fewer appeals. A proposed first phase would cover three life events before expanding.

## What Makes It New

Most government services wait for people to apply. This proposal reverses the direction: the government would come to the citizen at the moment of need, which is rare in social services.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the share of eligible families receiving support, the time from life event to first payment, and citizen satisfaction. A planned comparison with the current application route would test whether uptake improves.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in and a clear record of which data was used. Wrong eligibility decisions would be reduced by keeping a human review step for edge cases.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed early wellbeing check for students that would use a short, private monthly questionnaire to help school counsellors spot students who may be struggling, before problems become serious.

## Problem

Mental health difficulties among young people often go unnoticed until they affect attendance, grades, or safety. School counsellors have many students and few ways to know who needs help first.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Students aged 12 to 18 in public schools, their parents, and school counsellors.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes a five-minute monthly questionnaire on a school device, based on validated wellbeing questions. Answers would be seen only by the counsellor, who would receive a prioritised list of students to check in with. Students could also request a conversation directly through the tool.

## Delivery Model

Delivered through schools, with training for counsellors and a clear referral path to health services for serious cases.

## Funding & Sustainability

The plan is to fund it from the education wellbeing budget.

## What Makes It New

It turns wellbeing support from reactive to early and gives counsellors a way to prioritise.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the number of students supported early, counsellor response times, and student-reported wellbeing over the school year.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy concerns from parents are a major risk; the initiative plans parental consent, strict data access rules, and no link to grades or discipline records.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed service that would detect water leaks inside homes from smart meter data and alert residents by SMS before they receive a high bill.

## Problem

Hidden leaks in homes waste large amounts of water and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing financial stress and disputes with the utility.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Households with smart water meters, especially elderly residents and families on low incomes for whom a surprise bill is a hardship.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes analysing hourly meter readings to spot continuous night-time water flow, which usually means a leak. Residents would receive an alert with simple steps to check for leaks and a link to book a subsidised plumber visit.

## Delivery Model

Delivered by the water utility through its existing meter data and customer channels.

## Funding & Sustainability

The plan is to fund the service from reduced water losses and fewer billing disputes.

## What Makes It New

It turns meter data that already exists into a protective service for residents.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include water saved, the number of leaks fixed after alerts, and the number of billing disputes.

## Risks & Mitigation

False alarms could annoy residents; the initiative plans to set a conservative detection threshold in a first phase.

## One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that automatically detects major life events—such as the birth of a child, job loss, retirement, or a hospital discharge requiring rehabilitation—and proactively offers eligible citizens a bundled package of support, including guided home-based therapies, without requiring a formal application.

## Problem
Many families who qualify for social and health support services never receive them because they do not know the services exist, the rules are hard to understand, or the application process requires navigating paperwork from several different entities. People facing difficult moments, such as after a stroke or major surgery, often need rehabilitation most at the precise time they have the least energy for complex administrative tasks.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A typical use case is a patient discharged after a knee replacement whose hospital discharge is registered as a life event; within days, they would receive a clear message outlining the rehabilitation and social support they qualify for, with a simple way to accept the help.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant social supports (like financial aid or childcare services) triggered by the same life event.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered by public hospital departments and relevant social agencies. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. The proactive offer and management of the bundled support package would be coordinated through a central digital channel, with SMS and a phone line maintained for those not comfortable with digital tools.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, and more efficient application processing. Savings from these avoided costs are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology and service integration.

## What Makes It New
While most government services wait for people to find and apply for help, this proposal reverses the direction: by linking life-event data (with consent), the government would proactively come to the citizen at their moment of need with a pre-configured bundle of support, including health rehabilitation. This combined approach of automatic, event-triggered outreach and home-based, digitally guided therapy is rare in public service delivery.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of eligible families receiving support, completion rates of prescribed rehabilitation plans, improvements in patient mobility scores, and the rate of hospital readmissions within 90 days. A planned comparison would test whether this proactive, bundled model improves uptake and outcomes compared to the current system where citizens must seek out each service separately.

# One-Sentence Summary
A proposed service that proactively identifies outdoor workers facing imminent heat-risk events and automatically offers them access to mandated rest breaks, cooled shelters, and relevant support, without requiring a manual application.

## Problem
Outdoor workers in construction, delivery, and landscaping face serious health risks during extreme heat. General weather warnings are not specific enough to a worksite, and many workers feel unable to stop and rest without losing income. People in these dangerous moments face the greatest need for protection at the time they may have the least capacity or knowledge to navigate complex safety rules and support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Construction workers, delivery riders, cleaners, and gardeners who work outdoors, and the small employers who hire them. A typical use case is a delivery rider whose work route is forecast to enter a high-heat-risk zone, and who would then receive a clear alert and an automatic notification of their eligibility for a paid rest break and the location of the nearest cooled shelter.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes linking existing government and licensed weather data, with appropriate worker and employer consent, so that eligibility for heat-safety protections could be checked in the background when a high-risk forecast is confirmed for a specific worksite or zone. The worker and their employer would receive a clear message explaining the triggered protections (such as mandatory rest breaks), the location of the nearest cooled rest shelter, and any related income-support provisions they qualify for. They could accept, decline the specific shelter location, or ask a human advisor for help. No new documentation would be requested when work and location data already exist in permitted systems.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered through a lightweight government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for workers and employers who are not digital. A small central team would maintain the heat-risk and eligibility rules, and each participating data entity (e.g., weather services, licensed employment platforms) would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative plans to be funded from the existing workplace safety and social support budgets, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced healthcare expenditures and fewer workplace injury claims. A proposed first phase would cover two high-risk heat scenarios before expanding to other weather-related hazards.

## What Makes It New
Most government safety programs issue general warnings and rely on workers or employers to know and claim their rights. This proposal reverses the direction: the system would proactively identify the at-risk worker and come to them at the moment of imminent danger with specific, actionable protections, which is rare in occupational health services.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of at-risk workers who receive and use triggered protections, the time from heat-risk alert to first rest-break compliance, and worker satisfaction. A planned comparison with areas using only general warnings would test whether health outcomes improve.

## Risks & Mitigation
Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in for data linkage and a clear record of which data was used for the alert. Wrong risk or eligibility decisions would be mitigated by keeping a human review step for edge cases and complex employment situations.

# One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively detects household utility emergencies, such as hidden water leaks, by analyzing smart meter data and, for eligible families experiencing major life events, automatically offers a bundled package of support including guided home-based therapies and financial relief, without requiring a formal application.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A typical use case is a household on a low income where a hidden leak is detected; because the household is also identified as containing a patient recently discharged after a stroke, the residents would receive an alert and be automatically presented with a bundled package of support.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as options for subsidized repair, bill relief, or financial aid.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A small central team would maintain the rules linking utility data alerts and life-event data to support eligibility. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. Each participating entity (utilities, hospital departments, and government agencies) would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water). Savings from these avoided costs are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology, service integration, and the streamlined support.

## What Makes It New
Most government services wait for people to apply, especially after a crisis has already caused financial harm. This proposal reverses the direction: by fusing operational data (like meter readings) with social support systems, the government would come to the citizen at the moment a hidden emergency is detected and proactively offer a pre-configured bundle of support. This combined approach of automatic, data-triggered outreach and bundled, home-based therapy is rare in public service delivery.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of eligible households receiving support after an alert, completion rates of prescribed rehabilitation plans, improvements in patient mobility scores, the rate of hospital readmissions within 90 days, water saved, and the number of billing disputes avoided. A planned comparison would test whether this proactive, bundled model improves uptake, health outcomes, and reduces financial stress compared to the current system where citizens must seek out each service separately after discovering a crisis.
